editorial:
Imagine stepping back in time to see a legend at work. You get to hang out with Walt Disney himself as he walks you through his wildest dreams for the future. The vibe is super positive and full of energy, making you feel like you are in on a huge secret. It is not your typical movie, but it feels like a personal conversation with a man who wanted to change how people lived. You will see a side of Walt that is passionate and focused, showing off blueprints for a city that never quite happened the way he planned.

What really hits home is seeing the quality of the old footage and hearing Walt's voice right before he passed away. The pacing is quick, and the visuals of the planned city are still pretty cool to look at. The only downside is that it is a short film, so you might wish it were longer. If you love history or theme parks, you have to see this. It is a great idea to track down a high-quality 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection so you can see every detail of those vintage maps and models clearly.
endingExplained: The film wraps up with Walt giving a final, hopeful pitch about how his city of tomorrow will help people live better lives. He ends by explaining that this project is the next big step for his company. Since this was filmed just before he died, the ending feels bittersweet. You realize that the version of EPCOT he describes is very different from the theme park that actually exists today, leaving you to wonder what would have happened if he had lived.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Disney history or urban planning.
